title: Autorehearse promote controller with multi‑arm safety credits
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Adds an autorehearsal step to staged promotes that replays sampled live traffic into a dry-run cohort and computes per-arm safety credits; exposes a rollout advisory metric and a rollback credit ledger. Backwards compatible with existing rollout specs. Requires config opt-in and is feature-flagged.
description: Motivation: Reduce risky promotes by exercising candidate variants against a rehearsal harness before any traffic cutover. This PR introduces an 'autorehearse' step in the promote controller that replays sampled requests against candidate model variants (dry-run) to estimate latency/correctness regressions and compute a multi-arm safety credit score. The safety credits act as a conservative rollback budget used by the promote planner to decide whether to advance, hold, or abort. Key features: 1) Rehearsal harness that can run lightweight replay using prefix-sampled traffic (configurable reservoir). 2) Per-arm safety credit calculation based on latency P95, error delta, and fidelity checks against golden prompts. 3) Integration with the rollout planner to gate phased promotes when credits fall below thresholds. 4) Rollback ledger and explainable advisor logs that record the reason for an automatic backout. 5) New telemetry metrics and an ops dashboard for per-promote rehearsal summaries. Design links: Linear ENG-8421 design doc and playbook, design sketch: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-8421/autorehearse-design. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed - [x] Rehearsal harness implemented - [x] Safety credit algorithm added - [x] Planner gates wired - [x] End-to-end unit and integration tests - [x] Docs and console UI snippets added - [x] Feature-flag gated and rollout-config opt-in Implementation notes: The controller will, when a promote with autorehearse=true is requested, snapshot a small traffic reservoir (default 500 samples) or use live sampling, replay the reservoir to candidate variants in parallel under a dry-run mode, collect telemetry, then score each arm into safety credits. Scoring gives weight to latency regressions (P95), model output drift heuristics (token-level edit distance against canonical outputs for golden prompts), and failure/error rates. Credits decay over time and are storable on the rollout object to persist across retries. Operationally the promote will only advance if aggregate credits for the target traffic fraction exceed the configured threshold. Rollback behaviour: if credits fall during a staged promote below the abort threshold, the controller will trigger an automated rollback with a detailed audit entry that includes sample diffs, latency histograms, and the deterministic reason code. Backwards compatibility: existing promotes without autorehearse remain unchanged. Feature rollout: gated behind rolloutConfig.autorehearse, disabled by default. Security and perf: Rehearsals run in dry-run namespace and respect quota and customer data controls; replay is sampled and rate-limited to minimize cost and avoid impact on production model caches. Related work: this PR builds on earlier rehearse and shadow frameworks and replaces ad-hoc manual dry runs with first-class controller wiring. Next steps: iterate on credit weighting, add per-customer KMS tagging for sensitive replay, and surface more explainability signals in the console.
